Hi Amit — thanks for the clear list. Short answers below that should be suitable for the questionnaire; I attached a one-page retention summary and I started a spreadsheet mapping Solstice requirements to Redwood controls.

1) Regions/data centers: Redwood Hosted operates in selectable cloud regions (US-West, US-East, EU-West (Ireland), EU-Central (Frankfurt)). For Hosted API customers, you can select region preference at the project level; we do not replicate inference request/response logs to other regions unless you opt into cross-region backups. For customers requiring EU-only processing, we can enable a region lock for the project (see SLA note).

2) Default retention: by default, we retain non-PII request metadata and anonymized telemetry for 30 days for debugging and performance analysis. Full request and response payloads (customer-included data) are retained for 90 days by default for Hosted API but can be configured to shorter windows (minimum 0 days) on an account-by-account basis via the Console and API. Backups and system snapshots that may include encrypted logs are retained for up to 45 days and are subject to our snapshot rotation policy.

3) Deletion timeline: For a tenant-initiated deletion request (account erasure), Redwood will: (a) mark object data for deletion immediately, (b) purge live data within 24–72 hours depending on load and sharding, (c) remove data from active backups within up to 30 days as backups are rotated; (d) after backup rotation, provide a deletion confirmation. For most Hosted API accounts, end-to-end deletion (including backups) completes within 30 days; if you require an accelerated schedule or an SLA-backed deletion window, we can include that in an addendum. We can provide a signed certificate of deletion on request.

4) Region lock & SLA: We offer a Data Residency Addendum that can be attached to enterprise contracts to guarantee region locking for Hosted projects (no cross-region replication of request/response payloads). That addendum can include an SLA for region enforcement and an accelerated deletion SLA (e.g., backup purge within X days) for an additional fee.

Thanks Camila — added a few legal-friendly tweaks below that mirror our standard Data Residency Addendum. I also clarified the deletion cert process. Proposed language that you can paste into Solstice's questionnaire: 

- Data residency and region locking: Redwood Inference provides region selection at the project level for Hosted API. When region locking is requested via the Data Residency Addendum, Redwood will not replicate request or response payloads to other regions or peers. Logs required for infrastructure health may be processed in the same region; any cross-region mirroring of telemetry requires explicit customer opt-in.

- Retention windows: By default, customer-included request/response payloads are retained for up to 90 days. Customers may configure retention windows via the Redwood Console or API to a minimum of 0 days. Encrypted system snapshots may persist for up to 45 days for recovery purposes; we offer accelerated snapshot purge timelines in contract for customers who require it.

- Erasure guarantees and certificate: Redwood supports tenant-initiated erasure. Once a request is submitted through the Console or Support portal, Redwood marks all live objects for deletion within 24–72 hours and removes them from active storage. Backup snapshot rotation procedures will remove the data within the backup retention window (standard: up to 30 days). Upon completion, Redwood can issue a signed Certificate of Erasure containing timestamps and the scopes purged. For cases requiring faster removal from backups, include the accelerated deletion SLA in the addendum.

If Solstice needs an explicit number for the backup purge (they typically ask 7/14/30), we usually offer 30 days standard, 14 days for elevated enterprise, and 7 days available on a dedicated/priority plan.
